_comment: Source of truth for tools/sync-clickup.js. Derived from docs/state.md and docs/trace.md. Each node's `clickupId` is written back by the sync script — never edit that field by hand, or the next run will create a duplicate instead of updating. `status` is `done` ONLY where the work is built AND verified against the specs; a parent holding any unfinished child is `in progress`, never `done`.

tasks.name: Project setup
tasks.description: Repository, runtime, database and documentation scaffolding. Spec-first: the constitution and specs 001-013 were written before any code, and every item below traces to a numbered requirement.

subtasks.name: Express 5 bootstrap and environment config
subtasks.description: src/app.controller.js mounts the module controllers, a catch-all 404 and a last-resort error handler. Config comes from backend/.env, which is gitignored; backend/.env.example lists every key with no values.

subtasks.name: MongoDB single-node replica set (rs0)
subtasks.description: A replica set is not optional here. Constitution II requires every mutation and its audit entry to commit atomically, and MongoDB only offers transactions on a replica set. A standalone mongod would silently drop that guarantee.

subtasks.name: Platform module — branches, departments, localised value lists
subtasks.description: Branch and Department models plus the admin-authored value lists. Every admin-authored label carries { ar, en } with both required (constitution I), so a half-translated list cannot be saved.

subtasks.name: Angular 22 app shell, lazy routes, auth interceptor
subtasks.description: Standalone components, signals, lazy-loaded feature routes, an HTTP interceptor attaching the bearer token and a guard redirecting to /login. No @angular/localize — the language switch is runtime, not a build-time locale.

subtasks.name: API documentation — OpenAPI and Postman
subtasks.description: swagger-jsdoc blocks live above the routes they describe, so a route and its documentation are edited together. Served at /api-docs, written to docs/openapi.json by `npm run docs:build`, converted to a Postman collection by `npm run docs:postman`. Undocumented routes are absent rather than guessed at.

tasks.name: Auth
tasks.description: Local authentication is built and verified. SSO is a MUST in spec 010 and is not built — the parent stays `in progress` rather than `done` because of it.

subtasks.name: Local login with JWT
subtasks.description: POST /auth/login (spec 010 FR-006, FR-007). bcrypt password hashing, signed JWT, bilingual refusal on bad credentials that does not reveal whether the email exists.

subtasks.name: Break-glass administrator
subtasks.description: E-07: a seeded administrator that exists so a locked-out system can be recovered. Credentials come from BREAKGLASS_EMAIL / BREAKGLASS_PASSWORD in .env and appear in no tracked file. Its every action is audited like any other.

subtasks.name: Roles re-read from the database on every request
subtasks.description: The token carries identity, never permissions. Roles are loaded per request, so revoking a role takes effect on the holder's next call instead of when their token happens to expire.

subtasks.name: Login screen
subtasks.description: Bilingual login, mirrored in Arabic with no RTL override sheet. Verified by screenshot in both languages.

subtasks.name: SSO — SAML / OIDC
subtasks.description: Spec 010 names SSO as a MUST. Nothing has been built for it and no stub pretends otherwise.
subtasks.blocker: No identity provider has been named by the client. Without an IdP there is no metadata endpoint, no attribute mapping onto branch and department, and no answer to whether an SSO identity may hold the break-glass role. Building against a guessed provider would have to be thrown away.

tasks.name: Users and roles
tasks.description: Users, and the role assignments that bind a role to a branch and a department. A role has no meaning on its own here — it is always scoped.

subtasks.name: User model and creation
subtasks.description: User identity, hashed credentials, preferred language. Names are user-authored and therefore single-language (constitution I), unlike the admin-authored labels which require both.

subtasks.name: Role assignment — role bound to a branch and department
subtasks.description: RoleAssignment is the join that makes the scope predicate possible: AGENT in branch A department X is a different grant from AGENT in branch B. Assignment and revocation are both audited.

subtasks.name: Role visibility on GET /user
subtasks.description: Listing users requires LEAD or above, and the list itself is scope-filtered. This is why the ticket list derives its assignee filter from the tickets it already loaded rather than calling GET /user — an AGENT would receive a 404-shaped refusal.

subtasks.name: Deactivation and reassignment of open work
subtasks.description: Deactivating a user who holds open tickets is undefined behaviour today.
subtasks.blocker: Spec 010 does not say what happens to a deactivated user's open tickets — whether they are reassigned to the department lead, unassigned, or held. Each choice changes what the ticket list shows and what the audit entry must record, so it is a client decision, not an implementation detail.

tasks.name: Scope and permissions
tasks.description: Constitution IV. Every read and every write applies a branch + department predicate server-side. Two of three scope levels are built; the third cannot be built from the specs as written.

subtasks.name: Branch and department predicate on every read and write
subtasks.description: Applied in the data layer, not in the controllers, so a new endpoint cannot forget it. This is one of the two things marked never-to-shortcut in this project.

subtasks.name: Out of scope answers 404, never 403
subtasks.description: A 403 would confirm that a record exists in another branch, which is itself the disclosure the predicate exists to prevent. The body is byte-identical to a genuine not-found. Documented prominently in the OpenAPI description so integrators do not treat 404 as deletion.

subtasks.name: Team scope level
subtasks.description: SPEC DEFECT. Team is referenced as a scope level but is not implementable as specified.
subtasks.blocker: SPEC DEFECT — 'Team' is used as a scope level across specs 001 and 010, but no spec defines what a Team is, who assigns membership, whether it nests inside a department or crosses departments, or what a team-scoped read returns. It cannot be built without the client defining the entity. Recorded rather than guessed at, because guessing here would silently widen or narrow every query.

tasks.name: Audit log
tasks.description: Constitution II. Every mutation writes an immutable audit entry, and the entry commits in the same transaction as the mutation — there is no window in which one exists without the other. The writer is built and verified; nothing reads it back yet.

subtasks.name: Audit entry written inside the mutation's transaction
subtasks.description: utils/audit.js takes the caller's session. If the audit entry cannot be written the whole mutation aborts and the request answers 500 (E-11) rather than reporting a success that left no trace. The second of the two never-shortcut rules.

subtasks.name: Append-only enforcement
subtasks.description: AS-08. Mongoose hooks refuse update and delete on the audit collection, so append-only is a property of the model rather than a convention reviewers have to police.

subtasks.name: audit:reconcile with a model coverage check
subtasks.description: `npm run audit:reconcile` reports orphaned entries and unaudited records. The coverage check originally read mongoose.modelNames(), which only lists models that happen to have been imported — new models were invisible and the report read clean while covering nothing. Models are now imported and registered explicitly, and the fault was verified by injection rather than assumed fixed.

subtasks.name: Audit log viewer
subtasks.description: The trail is written and reconcilable but has no interface; reading it today means querying MongoDB directly.
subtasks.blocker: No spec defines who may read the audit log or with what filters. Reading it is itself a cross-branch disclosure — entries name records the reader may not be scoped to see — so the scope predicate for the viewer has to be specified before it can be built safely.

tasks.name: Bilingual and Arabic typography
tasks.description: Constitution I. Arabic and English are peers, not a base language and a translation. Verified by screenshot in both directions.

subtasks.name: Runtime language switch, no @angular/localize
subtasks.description: A signal-backed dictionary and a translate pipe. @angular/localize would mean one build artefact per locale and a page reload to change language, which fails the peer-language requirement for a user who works in both.

subtasks.name: Cairo, self-hosted, unicode-range subsets
subtasks.description: Arabic rendered in a typeface chosen for Arabic rather than a Latin face with fallback glyphs. Self-hosted with per-subset unicode-range, so a Latin-only page never downloads the Arabic subset.

subtasks.name: Logical properties throughout — RTL mirrors with no override sheet
subtasks.description: ms-/me-/ps-/pe-/start/end everywhere, never ml-/mr-/pl-/pr-. Direction is set once on the root element and the whole layout mirrors. There is no rtl.css, because an override sheet is a second place to forget.

subtasks.name: Bilingual refusal messages { ar, en }
subtasks.description: Every error body carries both languages so the client renders rather than translates. Field names stay English; only human-readable text is translated. References, phone numbers and email addresses stay LTR in both directions.

tasks.name: Customers
tasks.description: Customer records, contact points, duplicate handling and the screens over them. One requirement (E-15) cannot be built until a channel exists.

subtasks.name: Customer model — bilingual split, scope fields
subtasks.description: Customer names are user-authored and single-language; the admin-authored labels around them are { ar, en }. Decision 16 records where that line falls and why storing a customer name in two languages would invite invented translations of real people's names.

subtasks.name: Create, search, detail and update
subtasks.description: All four scope-predicated. Search matches account reference, name and contact point, and returns only in-scope records — a customer in another branch does not appear as a partial result.

subtasks.name: Duplicate collision — 409 with a confirmCollision override
subtasks.description: Duplicates are surfaced rather than blocked: POST /customer answers 409 naming the matching records, and the same request with confirmCollision: true proceeds and records the override in the audit entry. Collisions outside the caller's scope come back as a count with no identities — enough to warn, not enough to disclose.

subtasks.name: Contact points — one primary per channel type
subtasks.description: Enforced by a unique partial index. The index originally collided with another on the same key path and mongoose warned that `unique` would not be applied — the constraint would have silently not existed. Fixed with an explicit index name, one_primary_per_channel_type.

subtasks.name: Customer list, detail and create screens
subtasks.description: List with scope-aware search, detail with contact points, create with the collision dialogue wired to the 409 body. Verified by screenshot in both languages.

subtasks.name: Outbound refusal on a shared contact point
subtasks.description: E-15: refusing to send outbound to a contact point shared by more than one customer.
subtasks.blocker: Depends on an outbound channel existing. Nothing can be sent until spec 003 is built, so there is nothing yet for this rule to refuse. Building the check now would leave an untestable branch guarding a code path that does not exist.

tasks.name: Tickets
tasks.description: The ticket lifecycle: model, transition graph, references, assignment and the screens over them. Two items wait on client data or on the SLA engine.

subtasks.name: Ticket model, status set and transition graph
subtasks.description: Statuses and their legal transitions are data, not scattered conditionals. An illegal move is refused with 409 naming the reachable statuses.

subtasks.name: Ticket reference sequence
subtasks.description: A human-quotable reference allocated from a counter inside the creating transaction, so a rolled-back create burns no reference and two concurrent creates cannot share one. Always rendered LTR, in Arabic too.

subtasks.name: Create, list and filter, detail
subtasks.description: Scope-predicated throughout. GET /ticket/:id returns reachableStatuses so clients drive their controls from server truth instead of a hardcoded list.

subtasks.name: Assignment and status transition
subtasks.description: Both audited, both refusing assignment to a user outside the ticket's scope with the same 404 shape as any other out-of-scope reference.

subtasks.name: Ticket list, detail and create screens
subtasks.description: The status control is built from GET /ticket/:id's reachableStatuses and the pause-SLA flag from /ticket/meta. An earlier version hardcoded three statuses as pausing the clock — the same duplication-of-server-truth this project exists to avoid — and was replaced.

subtasks.name: Root cause and resolution code lists
subtasks.description: FR-029 requires both lists on ticket closure.
subtasks.blocker: The client has not supplied the values. These lists are the vocabulary every future report groups by, so inventing plausible-looking codes would seed the reporting module with fabricated taxonomy that nobody would later recognise as invented.

subtasks.name: Elapsed time on a ticket
subtasks.description: utils/elapsed-time.js exists and deliberately returns { status: 'unavailable' }.
subtasks.blocker: Blocked on spec 005. Constitution III makes elapsed-time.js the single source of every duration, and it stays unavailable until the SLA engine defines what pauses the clock. Nothing else in the codebase subtracts two dates — an 'obvious' created-to-now subtraction would be wrong the moment pauses exist, and wrong silently.

tasks.name: UI design system
tasks.description: Tailwind v4 alone, after a component library was installed and then removed. See decision 24.

subtasks.name: Tailwind v4 @theme tokens — colour, type scale, spacing
subtasks.description: CSS-first configuration via @theme in styles.css: no tailwind.config.js, one place where a token is defined and consumed.

subtasks.name: No component library — decision 24
subtasks.description: PrimeNG v22 injects a licence banner through a closed shadow root that cannot be removed from application code, and the v21 pin peer-depends on Angular 21 against this app's 22.1.5. Removed entirely and recorded as a decision headed DO NOT REINSTALL, so the next person does not rediscover it.

subtasks.name: Shared shell, table, form and status primitives
subtasks.description: The shell, tables, form controls and the status-tone pipe that colours a status chip. pending_internal is deliberately not amber: amber reads as paused, and that status does not pause the clock (decision 15).

tasks.name: Email channel
tasks.description: Spec 003. Inbound and outbound email threaded onto tickets.
tasks.blocker: Spec 003 is not built. There is no mailbox, no IMAP/SMTP credentials, and no decision on threading identity — whether a reply is matched by Message-ID and References headers or by a ticket reference stamped into the subject. The two behave differently when a customer forwards a thread, so the choice cannot be deferred to implementation.

tasks.name: WhatsApp channel
tasks.description: Spec 003. WhatsApp Business messaging bound to customer contact points.
tasks.blocker: Spec 003 is not built. Requires a WhatsApp Business API provider account and pre-approved message templates, neither of which exists. The 24-hour customer-service window also constrains when an agent may reply at all, which has no equivalent in any other channel and is unspecified here.

tasks.name: SMS channel
tasks.blocker: Spec 003 is not built. No SMS gateway has been chosen, and delivery in Saudi Arabia requires a registered sender ID that the client must obtain. Inbound SMS also has no threading key beyond the phone number, which is exactly the shared-contact-point case E-15 refuses.

tasks.name: Live chat
tasks.description: Spec 003. Real-time chat with an agent.
tasks.blocker: Spec 003 is not built. Needs a websocket transport, which nothing in the current stack provides, and an agent availability model that no spec defines. What happens to a chat started when no agent is available — queue, offline form, or refusal — is undecided, and it determines whether a chat can exist without a ticket.

tasks.name: SLA engine and automation
tasks.description: Spec 005. Response and resolution targets, pause semantics, escalation and time-based automation.
tasks.blocker: Spec 005 is not built, and it blocks every duration in the product. Constitution III makes utils/elapsed-time.js the sole source of elapsed time, and it returns { status: 'unavailable' } until this engine defines which statuses pause the clock and how working hours and holidays are handled. Reports (spec 009) are blocked behind this as well as behind their own spec.

tasks.name: Knowledge base
tasks.description: Spec 006. Articles agents can search and attach to a ticket.
tasks.blocker: Spec 006 is not built. Article scope is unresolved: whether an article is branch-scoped like every other record in the system, or deliberately global. Global content would be the first exception to the scope predicate and needs to be an explicit client decision rather than an implementation convenience. Bilingual authoring rules are also open — whether an article may exist in one language only, unlike admin-authored labels which may not.

tasks.name: Customer portal
tasks.description: Spec 008. Customers viewing and raising their own tickets.
tasks.blocker: Spec 008 is not built. It requires customer-facing authentication, which has no spec at all — the existing scope predicate is built around a staff identity holding a branch and department, and a customer identity holds neither. A portal cannot reuse the current authorisation model, so this is a new access model rather than a new set of screens.

tasks.name: Reports and management
tasks.description: Spec 009. Volume, workload, SLA attainment and resolution analysis.
tasks.blocker: Spec 009 is not built, and it is doubly blocked: most of the figures worth reporting are durations, which wait on the SLA engine (spec 005), and the grouping dimensions wait on the root-cause and resolution code lists the client has not supplied. A report built now could count tickets and nothing else.

tasks.name: ERP integration
tasks.description: Spec 011. Customer and order data read from the client's ERP.
tasks.blocker: Spec 011 is not built. No ERP product has been named, no endpoint supplied and no field mapping agreed — including the one that matters most, which system owns the customer record when both hold one. Until that is decided, an integration would be guessing at both the transport and the direction of truth.

tasks.name: AI features
tasks.description: Spec 007. Summarisation, classification and reply suggestion.
tasks.blocker: Spec 007 is not built, and it is blocked behind the channels (spec 003) rather than behind its own spec: every AI feature described operates on message content, and until a channel exists there are no messages to summarise, classify or reply to. Data handling is also unresolved — whether customer message content may leave the client's infrastructure is a decision the client has not been asked to make.
